records.name: Ad-Hoc Notebook-to-Production
records.definition: Promoting exploratory notebook code straight to production without engineering it into a reliable pipeline.

records.name: Deploy-and-Forget Models

distinctFrom.reason: Deploy-and-forget is never watching a model after release, while model drift is the loss of fidelity that goes unseen as a result.

records.definition: Deploying a model and never monitoring it, so degradation as the data drifts goes unnoticed.

records.name: Exact Keyword Search Only
records.definition: Relying solely on exact keyword matching for retrieval, missing semantically related results.

records.name: Flat Document-Only Knowledge
records.definition: Representing knowledge as unlinked flat documents, losing the relationships a graph would capture.

records.name: Opaque Black-Box Decisions
records.definition: Producing model decisions with no explanation, so their reasoning cannot be inspected or trusted.

records.name: Opaque Ungoverned Model Use
records.definition: Using models with no governance or oversight, leaving their behavior and risks unmanaged.

records.name: Training-Time-Only Model Logic
records.definition: Building logic that exists only during training, with no counterpart to serve predictions at inference.

records.name: Unapproved Model Deployment

distinctFrom.reason: Unapproved deployment skips the approval gate, while version ambiguity loses track of which version and configuration is running.

records.definition: Deploying a model to production without passing the required review and approval gates.

records.name: Ungrounded Generation
records.definition: Generating output from a model alone without grounding it in retrieved facts, inviting hallucination.

records.name: Unguarded Model Autonomy
records.definition: Letting a model act autonomously with no safety guardrails on what it can do.

records.name: Untested Model Deployment
records.definition: Deploying a model without evaluating it, so its real-world quality is unknown until it fails.

records.name: Approval Policy
records.definition: The declared rules and gates a model must pass before it may be deployed.

records.name: Document Store
records.definition: The body of documents a retrieval system searches to ground a model's generation.

records.name: Data Pipeline
records.definition: The stages that ingest, clean, and transform data into a form suitable for training or inference.

records.name: Data/Model Boundaries
records.definition: The lines separating data preparation, model training, and serving so each concern stays isolated.

records.name: Dataset
records.definition: A curated collection of examples used to train or evaluate a model.

records.name: Embeddings

distinctFrom.reason: Embeddings are the vectors themselves, while a vector index organizes them for nearest-neighbor lookup.

records.definition: Numeric vector representations of data that place semantically similar items near each other.

records.name: Entities

distinctFrom.reason: Entities are a knowledge graph's nodes, while relations are its edges.
Entities are the instances in the graph, while the schema defines the entity types they belong to.

records.definition: The distinct things, such as people, places or concepts, that a knowledge graph represents as nodes.

records.name: Grounding Strategy
records.definition: A scheme for anchoring a model's output in retrieved, authoritative sources rather than its parameters alone.

records.name: Guardrails
records.definition: Constraints and filters that bound what a model is permitted to output or do at runtime.

records.name: Input/Output Contract
records.definition: The agreed schema of the inputs a model accepts and the outputs it returns.

records.name: Model Artifact
records.definition: The trained model file, with its learned weights, that is loaded to serve predictions.

records.name: Model Registry
records.definition: A catalog that tracks model versions, their metadata, and their deployment status.

records.name: Rationale/Evidence
records.definition: The reasons and supporting evidence recorded for a model's decision.

records.name: Relations

distinctFrom.reason: Relations are the edges present in the graph, while the schema defines the relationship types allowed.

records.definition: The typed connections between entities that a knowledge graph represents as edges.

records.name: Retriever
records.definition: A component that finds and returns the most relevant documents for a query.

records.name: Schema/Ontology
records.definition: A formal definition of the entity types and relationship types a knowledge graph may contain.

records.name: Tool Interface
records.definition: The defined contract through which an agent invokes external tools and receives their results.

records.name: Training/Inference Separation
records.definition: The requirement that model training and prediction serving be distinct, separately-managed phases.

records.name: Vector Index
records.definition: A data structure that organizes embedding vectors for fast nearest-neighbor lookup.

records.name: Retraining Triggers
records.definition: Signals that automatically initiate model retraining when measured drift crosses a threshold.

records.name: Model-Integrated Systems
records.definition: The ability of a software system to incorporate models as integral parts of its behavior.

records.name: Audit and Debugging
records.definition: The ability to inspect and trace a model's decisions for auditing and debugging.

records.name: Bounded Tool-Using Agents

distinctFrom.reason: Bounded tool use limits which tools an agent may call, while governed autonomy limits which decisions it may take without approval.

records.definition: The ability to run agents that use external tools within defined, safe limits.

records.name: Contextual Generation
records.definition: The ability to generate output informed by retrieved, task-specific context.

records.name: Controlled Model Deployment
records.definition: The ability to release models through a governed, approved process.

records.name: Degradation Detection
records.definition: The ability to detect when a model's accuracy declines as data shifts.

records.name: Governed Autonomy
records.definition: The ability to let an agent act autonomously within enforced governance limits.

records.name: Model Selection/Regression Detection
records.definition: The ability to compare models and catch quality regressions before deployment.

records.name: Relationship-Aware Retrieval/Reasoning
records.definition: The ability to retrieve and reason over the relationships between entities, not just isolated facts.

records.name: Reliable Model Lifecycle
records.definition: The ability to manage a model's data, training, deployment and monitoring reliably and repeatably.

records.name: Safe Model Deployment
records.definition: The ability to deploy models with safeguards that bound their behavior.

records.name: Semantic Search
records.definition: The ability to find results by meaning and similarity rather than exact keyword match.

records.name: Similarity Retrieval
records.definition: The ability to retrieve items nearest to a query in an embedding space.

records.name: Structured, Versioned Prompts
records.definition: Prompts authored as structured, version-controlled artifacts rather than ad-hoc strings.

records.name: Knowledge Freshness
records.definition: The degree to which a system's knowledge reflects current rather than stale information.

records.name: Trust
records.definition: The degree to which users are willing to rely on a system's outputs.

records.name: Capability/Utility
records.definition: The degree of usefulness a model offers, which strict safety limits can constrain.

records.name: Curation Cost
records.definition: The degree of ongoing effort required to build and maintain a curated knowledge graph.

records.name: Experiment Velocity
records.definition: The rate at which model experiments can be run and iterated, which governance can slow.

records.name: Experimentation Speed
records.definition: The rate at which new modeling ideas can be tried and evaluated.

records.name: Explainability/Recall
records.definition: The degree to which retrieval stays explainable and complete, traded against pure similarity ranking.

records.name: Latency/Cost
records.definition: The degree of latency and expense incurred to serve model predictions.

records.name: Metric Completeness
records.definition: The degree to which evaluation metrics capture every dimension of a model's quality.

records.name: Model Complexity
records.definition: The degree of intricacy in a model, which raises accuracy but lowers explainability.

records.name: Monitoring Cost
records.definition: The degree of ongoing expense of continuously monitoring a deployed model.

records.name: Retrieval Quality/Latency
records.definition: The degree to which retrieval must trade result quality against speed.

records.name: Prompt Registry
records.definition: A technique for keeping prompts in one versioned registry instead of as literals across the code.

records.name: Prompt Versioning
records.definition: A technique for giving each prompt, dataset and index a version that inference logs record.

records.name: Evaluation Suite
records.definition: A technique for scoring model output against a fixed set of cases on every change to the model, prompt or data.

records.name: Centralized Model Configuration
records.definition: A technique for holding model names, parameters and limits in one configuration read by every call site.

records.name: Inference Context Record
records.definition: A technique for logging with each model output the model version, prompt version and inputs that produced it.

records.name: Evidence Citation
records.definition: A technique for attaching to each generated claim the retrieved source that supports it.

records.name: Claim Validation
records.definition: A technique for checking generated claims against their cited sources before they are returned.

records.name: Abstain or Disclose Uncertainty
records.definition: A technique for having a model decline or state its uncertainty when the evidence does not support an answer.

records.name: Governance Log
records.definition: A technique for recording each approval, deployment and retirement of a model with who decided it.
